meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще').

examples.text: Катя, подожди, это вообще кто?
examples.trans: Katya, wait, who on earth is this?

examples.text: Здесь вообще-то люди ходят.
examples.trans: People actually walk through here.

examples.text: Папа, у тебя совесть вообще есть?
examples.trans: Dad, do you have any conscience at all?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to change; to swap', paired with 'поменять'.

examples.text: У меня в молодости такой мотоцикл был.
examples.trans: I had a motorcycle like that in my youth.

examples.text: У меня такой в мастерской стоит.
examples.trans: I have one like that standing in my workshop.

examples.text: Меня зовут Виктор, а тебя?
examples.trans: My name is Viktor, and yours?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'maybe', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Давление, наверное, может, я дома отлежусь?
examples.trans: It is probably blood pressure, maybe I can rest at home?

examples.text: Может, ты сможешь с ними спокойно поговорить?
examples.trans: Maybe you can talk to them calmly?

examples.text: Может быть, нам лучше полицию вызвать?
examples.trans: Maybe we had better call the police?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'better', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ничего не случится, спокойно обойдут.
examples.trans: Nothing will happen, they can walk around it.

examples.text: Вчера как-то неудобно у нас получилось.
examples.trans: Things turned out rather awkwardly between us yesterday.

examples.text: Катя, не слушай его, он хотел получить деньги!
examples.trans: Katya, do not listen to him, he wanted to get money!

meanings.note: Borrowed in the Petrine era from German 'Polizei' / French 'police' (from Greek 'politeia', civil administration).

examples.text: Может быть, нам лучше полицию вызвать?
examples.trans: Maybe we had better call the police?

examples.text: Звони в полицию!
examples.trans: Call the police!

examples.text: Полиция здесь.
examples.trans: The police are here.

meanings.en: to call for, to summon (a taxi, driver, police, doctor)
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'звать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to call, to summon', paired with 'вызывать'.

examples.text: Может быть, нам лучше полицию вызвать?
examples.trans: Maybe we had better call the police?

examples.text: Ты вызвал трезвого водителя!
examples.trans: You called a sober driver!

examples.text: Мы сразу вызвали скорую помощь.
examples.trans: We immediately called an ambulance.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нет, тогда тебе ещё хуже будет.
examples.trans: No, then it will be even worse for you.

examples.text: Да не сопротивляйся, у меня нет времени!
examples.trans: Stop resisting, I have no time!

examples.text: Нет, ты так хорошо ей подходишь, сынок!
examples.trans: No, you suit her so well, son!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'else/more', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ещё раз опоздаешь, без зарплаты останешься.
examples.trans: Be late one more time and you will be left without a paycheck.

examples.text: У тебя ещё есть вопросы?
examples.trans: Do you have any more questions?

examples.text: А у тебя ещё дочки есть?
examples.trans: Do you have any more daughters?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('worse').

examples.text: Нет, тогда тебе ещё хуже будет.
examples.trans: No, then it will be even worse for you.

examples.text: Всё гораздо хуже.
examples.trans: It's much worse.

examples.text: Сегодня хуже, чем вчера.
examples.trans: Today is worse than yesterday.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'go, walk', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.text: Я иду домой.
examples.trans: I'm going home.

examples.text: Он идёт на второй срок.
examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: to talk, to speak, to have a conversation
meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'говаривать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'talk'.

examples.text: Иди разговаривай, я им слово дал!
examples.trans: Go talk to them, I gave them my word!

examples.text: Почему вы так грубо разговариваете?
examples.trans: Why are you talking so rudely?

examples.text: Мы разговариваем.
examples.trans: We're talking.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лово'). Common neuter noun meaning 'word' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Хватит бить, ты мне позвоночник сломаешь!
examples.trans: Stop hitting me, you will break my spine!

examples.text: Иди разговаривай, я им слово дал!
examples.trans: Go talk to them, I gave them my word!

examples.text: Поэтому я от души благословляю вас.
examples.trans: Therefore I bless you from the bottom of my heart.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give', paired with 'давать'.

examples.text: Эй, герой, сколько тебя ещё ждать?
examples.trans: Hey, hero, how much longer do we have to wait for you?

examples.text: Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: Give me just one.

examples.text: Дайте, пожалуйста, воды.
examples.trans: Some water, please.
